## Tutorials

The LOWER() function converts a string to lower-case.

Note:TheLCASE()function is equal to the LOWER() function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LOWER("SQL Tutorial is FUN!");

---

LOWER(
text
)

---

SELECT LOWER(CustomerName) AS LowercaseCustomerName
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The LPAD() function left-pads a string with another string, to a certain 
length.

Note:Also look at theRPAD()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LPAD("SQL Tutorial", 
  20, "ABC");

---

LPAD(
string
,
length
,
lpad_string
)

---

SELECT LPAD(CustomerName, 30, "ABC") AS LeftPadCustomerName
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The LTRIM() function removes leading spaces from a string.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LTRIM("     SQL Tutorial") AS LeftTrimmedString;

---

LTRIM(
string
)
```

## Tutorials

The MID() function extracts a substring from a string (starting at any position).

Note:The position of the first character in the string is 1.

Note:The position of the last character in the string is -1.

Note:The MID() andSUBSTR()functions 
equals theSUBSTRING()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT MID("SQL Tutorial", 5, 3) AS ExtractString;

---

MID(
string
,
start
,
length
)

---

SELECT MID(CustomerName, 
  2, 5) AS ExtractString
FROM Customers;

---

SELECT MID("SQL Tutorial", -5, 5) AS ExtractString;
```

## Tutorials

The POSITION() function returns the position of the first occurrence of a substring 
in a string.

If the substring is not found within the original string, this function returns 0.

This function performs a case-insensitive search.

Note:TheLOCATE()function is 
equal to the 
POSITION() function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT POSITION("3" IN "W3Schools.com") AS MatchPosition;

---

POSITION(
substring
IN
string
)

---

SELECT POSITION("COM" IN "W3Schools.com") AS MatchPosition;

---

SELECT POSITION("a" IN CustomerName)
FROM Customers;
```
